Hi Antonio,

Congrats on the new funding (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/exclusive-seltz-startup-rebuilding-search-110000196.html?fr=sycsrp_catchall).
I'd like to use Seltz and send you one concrete thing I'd build or fix: [after trying it: one specific observation].

I came across Seltz: A search engine built for AI agents that crawls the web, indexes it, and returns machine‑ready passages, tables and images instead of human‑focused snippets.
Saw the recent news (raised money (13d ago)).
One thing I noticed: Scaling the crawling and indexing pipeline to keep sub‑200 ms latency while handling hundreds of millions of pages daily.

You could offload the heavy lifting of real‑time retrieval to a Next.js front‑end backed by a vector semantic search layer, dramatically cutting latency for AI agents.

Would a short trial project to tackle this be useful?

If this isn't relevant, just reply "no" and I won't follow up.
